title: Prompt Anatomy and Success Criteria
summary: Turn an ambiguous request into a clear, testable working agreement with an AI system.
objectives: Separate a prompt's purpose, inputs, instructions, constraints, deliverable, and verification.
Define observable success criteria before generating an answer.
Distinguish hard requirements from preferences and examples.
Rewrite an ambiguous request as a reusable prompt template.

sections.title: Start with the outcome and its user
paragraphs: A prompt is easier to follow when it names the outcome, the person who will use it, and the decision or action it should support. A topic such as “customer feedback” is not yet a task; “group these comments so the support lead can choose three fixes” is.

Purpose helps the model choose relevant detail, but it also helps the learner decide whether AI is appropriate. If the intended use is high impact, private, or irreversible, the prompt must include stronger evidence and review boundaries.
sections.callout: Describe the useful result, not only the subject.

sections.title: Name trusted inputs and explicit instructions
paragraphs: Identify the material the response may rely on and label its boundaries. Separate instructions from source text, examples, and user-supplied data so quoted material is not mistaken for a command.
Use ordered steps when sequence matters. State what to do with missing or conflicting inputs rather than allowing the system to silently invent a resolution.

code.label: Purpose-first prompt template
code.code:
Purpose: [OUTCOME AND USER]
Inputs: [TRUSTED MATERIAL AND BOUNDARIES]
Instructions:
1. [FIRST REQUIRED ACTION]
2. [NEXT REQUIRED ACTION]
Constraints: [MUST, MUST NOT, PRIVACY, SCOPE]
Deliverable: [FORMAT AND DETAIL]
Verify: [CHECKS AND EVIDENCE]
If information is missing: [ASK, FLAG, OR STOP]

sections.title: Make success observable
paragraphs: Success criteria describe what a reviewer can inspect: required fields are present, claims map to supplied evidence, calculations reproduce, links resolve, or a stated rubric is satisfied. “Make it excellent” does not identify an observable result.
Separate hard requirements from preferences. A hard requirement can fail the result; a preference guides style when it does not conflict with the required outcome.

sections.title: Design for missing information and uncertainty
paragraphs: A useful prompt tells the system when to ask a question, state an assumption, identify uncertainty, or stop. This prevents a polished response from hiding an unsupported choice.
Prompting improves the odds of a useful response, but it does not guarantee truth. The prompt should name the verification that happens after generation.
sections.callout: A good prompt defines how to fail visibly.

activity.title: Rewrite an ambiguous request
instructions: Choose a vague request such as “summarize this,” “make a plan,” or “compare these tools.”
Identify its user, intended decision, trusted inputs, hard constraints, and observable success criteria.
Rewrite it with the purpose-first template and include behavior for missing or conflicting information.
Ask another person to identify anything they would still have to guess.
evidence: The original request and a completed prompt containing purpose, inputs, instructions, constraints, deliverable, verification, and missing-information behavior.
A short review listing at least one ambiguity removed and one remaining assumption.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which missing detail changed the task most when you made it explicit?

cues.text: Contrast a topic with an outcome that names the user and decision it supports.
Transform the words customer feedback into outcome, user, and decision cards.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A text sequence expands customer feedback into: outcome—group comments; user—support lead; decision—choose three fixes. Reduced-motion mode shows all cards at once.

cues.text: Explain why instructions, trusted inputs, quoted text, and examples need visible boundaries.
Pause while learners label each field in the purpose-first template with information from a task they know.
Allow ninety seconds for learners to separate source material from instructions.
Replace subjective wishes with evidence a reviewer can observe and distinguish requirements from preferences.
Show how ask, flag, assume, and stop policies make uncertainty visible instead of silently filling gaps.
Check that the learner can name one observable success criterion and one visible failure behavior.
Guide the learner through rewriting their ambiguous request and peer-checking what remains unclear.
Invite the learner to take the check after every field in the rewritten prompt is testable or intentionally optional.

questions.prompt: Which request states the clearest purpose?
choices: Write about customer feedback
Group the supplied comments so the support lead can choose three fixes
Make this better
Think very carefully
questions.explanation: It names the material, user, action, and decision the output supports.

questions.prompt: Why should source text be separated from instructions?
choices: To reduce the chance that quoted or untrusted text is treated as a command
To make the prompt longer
To guarantee every claim is true
To hide the source from the reviewer
questions.explanation: Visible boundaries clarify which content directs the task and which content is data to analyze.

questions.prompt: Which is an observable success criterion?
choices: The answer feels brilliant
The model tries its best
The answer includes each required field and maps every factual claim to a supplied source
The response sounds confident
questions.explanation: A reviewer can inspect required fields and claim-to-source mappings.

questions.prompt: What should a prompt do when required context is missing?
choices: Always invent a plausible value
Remove the success criteria
Treat the missing value as private
Define whether to ask, flag an assumption, or stop
questions.explanation: An explicit missing-information policy prevents silent unsupported choices.

questions.prompt: Which statement about prompting is accurate?
choices: A detailed prompt guarantees factual correctness
Prompt quality matters, but important outputs still require verification
Only provider-specific prompts can be evaluated
Examples eliminate the need for instructions
questions.explanation: Clear prompts improve task execution; they do not remove model uncertainty or the need to verify consequential work.
